samples.text:
The table gives information about six big cities and it shows there population, area and population density.

Lagos had the biggest population with 15.4 million people, and Tokyo was next with 14.0 million. Mumbai had 12.5 million, while Cairo and Lima had 10.2 million and 10.0 million. Toronto was much smaller than the other cities, only 2.8 million people live there.

Looking at area, Cairo is the largest city with 3,085 km², and Lima and Tokyo are also big with 2,672 km² and 2,194 km². Lagos has 1,171 km², which is in the middle. Mumbai and Toronto are the smallest cities, 603 km² and 630 km².

About density, Mumbai is the most crowded city because it has 20,730 people per km². Lagos is second with 13,151. Tokyo has 6,381 and Toronto has 4,444. Lima and Cairo have the lowest density, 3,743 and 3,306 people per km².

Overall, Mumbai is the most dense city although it has small area, and Lagos have the most people.
samples.why: Accurate figures for all three measures · brief overview at the end · columns described separately with little link between area and density · tense, article and agreement errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table compares six major cities in terms of their population, land area and population density.

Overall, there were considerable differences between the cities. Lagos had the largest population, whereas Mumbai was by far the most densely populated city, because of its relatively small area. Toronto had the fewest inhabitants, while Cairo covered the largest area and had the lowest density.

With 15.4 million residents, Lagos was the most populous city, followed by Tokyo with 14.0 million and Mumbai with 12.5 million. Cairo and Lima had similar populations, at 10.2 million and 10.0 million respectively, while Toronto was much smaller at 2.8 million.

In terms of area, Cairo was the largest city at 3,085 km², followed by Lima (2,672 km²) and Tokyo (2,194 km²). Mumbai and Toronto occupied the smallest areas, at 603 km² and 630 km² respectively. Consequently, Mumbai had an exceptionally high density of 20,730 people per km², and Lagos also had a high figure of 13,151. In contrast, Tokyo's density was much lower at 6,381, despite its large population, and the remaining three cities had the lowest densities, ranging from 3,306 in Cairo to 4,444 in Toronto.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main extremes · link between area and density highlighted · logical progression · good range of vocabulary (populous, occupied) · frequent error-free sentences with slight overuse of respectively.

samples.text:
The table provides data on the population, land area and population density of six large cities.

The most striking feature is the variation in density, which depends as much on land area as on population size. Mumbai is by far the most crowded city despite occupying the smallest area, while Cairo, the largest city by area, is the least densely populated.

Lagos has the largest population, at 15.4 million, and because its area is a relatively compact 1,171 km², it has the second-highest density, at 13,151 people per km². Mumbai, with 12.5 million inhabitants living in just 603 km², is even more densely populated, with 20,730 people per km², more than six times the figure for Cairo.

Tokyo presents a contrasting case. Although its population of 14.0 million is the second largest, it is spread over 2,194 km², giving a moderate density of 6,381. Cairo and Lima, each with around ten million residents, cover the largest areas, at 3,085 km² and 2,672 km², so their densities are the lowest, at 3,306 and 3,743 respectively. Toronto is the smallest city by population, at only 2.8 million, but its limited area of 630 km² results in a density of 4,444, slightly higher than those of Cairo and Lima.
samples.why: Insightful overview linking density to area · features synthesised across columns with an accurate ratio · cohesion managed effortlessly · precise vocabulary (compact, populous) · wide range of structures, error-free.
